svg.title: Neutral atom qubits
svg.desc: The photographed Pasqal ORION cabinet houses an analog neutral-atom QPU. Optical tweezers set the atom layout; laser pulses drive Rydberg states, letting interacting atoms evolve together. Other neutral-atom platforms can implement digital gates.
svg.text: Inside the Pasqal ORION cabinet, focused beams of light hold individual atoms in place like tiny tweezers.
A laser can lift an atom to a higher energy level. That makes it harder for a nearby atom to do the same.
To program ORION, choose where the atoms sit and how the laser pulses. Then let the atoms interact.
This is analog computing: the atoms evolve together, and measuring their final pattern gives a result.
